description: Admin screens for Solhigson apps as Razor components, rendered on the server. An app owns its routes; the package ships no page.
releaseNotes: 10.7.0: the cache page and the root encryption page (Solhigson.Admin.Cache, Solhigson.Admin.Encryption, Solhigson.Admin.Components). The cache seam: IKitCache, which AddSolhigsonAdmin registers scoped as KitCache<TContext> over the app's identity context with either overload, keeping one the app registered first, resolves the context from the request's services at each resync. ResyncAsync calls the framework's ResyncCacheAndWaitAsync with a five-second wait (KitCache.WaitSeconds) and answers a KitCacheResult (TypeCount, ProviderPresent, Confirmed, Outcome, Message): a KitCacheOutcome (Resynced, Unconfirmed, NothingCached or Failed, and None, never answered) and KitCacheMessages' sentence for it. A fault, a context that does not resolve among them, is Failed with one KitCacheResyncFailed Error under Solhigson.Admin.Cache.KitCache naming the context's type and carrying the exception; nothing throws but the caller's cancellation. KitCacheResync (CanResync, AuditHref) is the cache page: a header, Cache, whose line says what a resync costs; with AuditHref, the audit page's path, a Past resyncs link to the audit list filtered to cache.resynced over all time; without CanResync, false unless set, a line saying resyncing needs the resync permission and no form, so a post gets the framework's 400; with it, one form, cache-resync, holding Resync cache, with no confirm. The handler checks CanResync itself, and the resync is not cancelled by the request, so a landed reset is always answered and recorded. One alert per outcome: Success with the count, Warn when other instances did not confirm within the wait, Neutral when nothing is cached, Danger on a fault; the page shows its own sentence, never the seam's Message. A Resynced or Unconfirmed resync is recorded through IKitAudit as cache.resynced (KitCacheAudit: entity type Cache, keyed cache, named the cache, its payload TypeCount and Confirmed), and the alert adds the resync was not recorded, in Warn, when the row was not written or IKitAudit records nothing. KitRootEncryption (CanReEncrypt, SettingsHref) is the root encryption page, over the framework's RootReEncryption census, read in the request with the request's cancellation: no RootReEncryption registered, or its NotRegisteredMessage, is the empty state Root encryption is not set up; any other failure a Danger alert, Root encryption could not be read, with the framework's message; else the header names the current key's id and check value and how many stored values are not under it, a Danger alert names each key with values that is not in configuration, and the tables Keys, Stores and Values that need attention follow, each value off the current key named with what is wrong in words, and with SettingsHref, the settings page's path, a setting's row links to the settings screen finding its name. Key ids and check values alone are rendered, never key material. Without CanReEncrypt, false unless set, a note says re-encrypting needs the re-encrypt permission; with it and a movable value, Re-encrypt under the current key opens one Primary confirm, root-re-encrypt (Re-encrypt <n> values), which runs RootReEncryption.ReEncryptAsync. The handler checks CanReEncrypt, the page's address and a movable value itself, and a post where the confirm did not render gets the framework's 400. The run is not cancelled by the request, so a closed tab never stops it half way; the page then reads the census again and shows Re-encrypted <n> values, Warn with the values skipped or unreadable, or a Danger alert, Re-encryption stopped, with the framework's message. The run observer: AddSolhigsonAdmin registers KitRootReEncryptionObserver scoped as the framework's IRootReEncryptionRunObserver with either overload, keeping one the app registered first. The framework tells it of every run, whoever started it, a stopped one included, and it records each through IKitAudit as encryption.re-encrypted, or encryption.re-encrypt-stopped for a run that stopped (KitEncryptionAudit: entity type RootEncryption, keyed root-encryption, named the stored secrets, its payload CurrentKeyId, the sums Converted, Skipped and Unreadable, StoppedAt and each store's counts, never a row's key), and writes one KitRootReEncryptStopped Warning under Solhigson.Admin.Encryption.KitRootReEncryptionObserver for a stopped run. The page says the run was not recorded when the row was not written, IKitAudit records nothing, no observer is registered or the observer could not be resolved. KitAuditLabels words the three actions: cache.resynced as Cache resynced (resynced), encryption.re-encrypted as Re-encryption run (ran re-encryption over) and encryption.re-encrypt-stopped as Re-encryption stopped (did not finish re-encrypting); TypeInWords reads Cache as cache and RootEncryption as root encryption. kit.manifest.json gains the kit-cache and kit-encryption components and the classes kit-cache, kit-encryption, kit-encryption-actions, kit-encryption-code, kit-encryption-key, kit-encryption-muted, kit-encryption-note, kit-encryption-open, kit-encryption-row, kit-encryption-section and kit-encryption-section-title, and loses none. To adopt: add the two pages, each with its route and [Permission], passing CanResync and CanReEncrypt from the app's own permission checks; throttle both routes, since the resync and the re-encrypt run each answer a post; for the root page, call AddRootEncryption and register the framework's own context (SolhigsonDbContext), which the app settings store reads; on a host with many enrolled users the census belongs in a job, since the page runs it in the request; hold the root page's view permission for operators only, since each load reads and decrypts every store; pass the audit list's address to the cache page as AuditHref. The README lists the lines the two pages, the cache seam and the run observer cause that an operator acts on (KitCacheResyncFailed, KitRootReEncryptStopped, the framework's resync, census, run and observer lines, the cache manager's Warnings, the permission refusal, and the audit lines of a lost record), each with its level and what to do. Changes for a 10.6.0 app: AddSolhigsonAdmin also registers IKitCache and IRootReEncryptionRunObserver, keeping each one the app registered first, so a re-encrypt run the app starts elsewhere, from a job among them, is now recorded through IKitAudit, and a stopped one writes KitRootReEncryptStopped; the audit screens word the three new actions and the two entity types, which they read as stored before; and the stylesheet's shared column, section, table, link, muted, actions, code and note rules also cover the two pages, with no rule changed for an existing class. No existing type gains a public member; IKitCache, KitCache, KitCacheResult, KitCacheOutcome, KitCacheMessages, KitCacheAudit, KitEncryptionAudit, KitCacheResync and KitRootEncryption are new. Minor bump. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.32.0 or later. 10.6.0: the log screens (Solhigson.Admin.Logs, Solhigson.Admin.Components): the application log screen, the application log record page, the API log screen and the API exchange page. The logs seam: IKitLogs, which AddSolhigsonAdmin registers scoped with either overload, keeping one the app registered first, reads the application log through the framework's IAppLogReader and the API exchanges through its IApiLogReader, each resolved from the request's services at its first use; AddSolhigsonLokiReader registers the ones that read Grafana Loki. Every member takes the viewer's principal first, and answers ActorRefused, reading nothing, for one that names no signed-in user. GetSourceAsync (KitLogKind App or Api) answers a KitLogSource: State, a KitLogSourceState (NotRegistered, Off, while the reader's ReadEnabled is false or the host does not export its API exchanges, or Ready), and Newest, a KitLogNewest of a KitLogNewestState and its time At. SearchAppLogsAsync (a KitAppLogSearch: FromDay, ToDay, Since, MinSeverity, RequestId, UserId, Cursor, Zone) and SearchApiLogsAsync (a KitApiLogSearch: FromDay, ToDay, Since, Service, Method, StatusCode, PathContains, RequestId, Cursor, Zone) answer a KitLogPage<T> (Rows, NextCursor, From, To, Offset, Since, ReadAt); GetAppLogAsync answers a KitLogLookup<AppLogRecord>, AppLogsOfRequestAsync a KitLogLookup<KitAppLogsOfRequest> (the request's first 50 records, oldest first, and More), and GetApiLogAsync a KitLogLookup<KitApiExchange>, whose RequestHeaders and ResponseHeaders are each a KitLogHeaders (Entries of KitLogHeader in the stored order, Stored when what is stored is not a JSON object, or None). Each answer carries a KitLogOutcome (Done, NotRegistered, Off, ActorRefused, NotConfigured, Unreachable, Refused, NotFound, Failed) and KitLogMessages' sentence for it, NotConfigured naming the setting's key; after an Unreachable, the request's later reads answer it without calling a reader, and nothing throws but the caller's cancellation. A window is UTC instants, the end exclusive: with days, from the viewer's midnight of the first day, placed at the zone's offset at that midnight, to the midnight after the last, capped at now; with none, the hour before Since or now, ending on a whole second. A request id that is not 32 hexadecimal characters, and a cursor the reader refuses, are dropped. A fault in the seam writes one KitLogsFailed Error naming the method, the step and the exception's type, and a viewer not signed in one KitLogsNoActor Warning; each call adds one to the counter logs and records its seconds on the histogram logs.duration, on the meter Solhigson.Admin (KitLogsDiagnostics), tagged method and outcome. The screens: each is a component on the app's own route, its addresses paths on the site that KitHref.Local accepts, and no value of a record is rendered as markup. KitAppLogList (DetailHref, TimeZone, StaleAfter, 15 minutes by default) lists the application log's records of one window, newest first, a page at a time, under the presets Last hour, Today and Last 7 days and a GET filter bar (from, to, severity, and the request id and user id under More filters), with a Warn alert when the newest record is older than StaleAfter or none came in 24 hours. KitApiLogList (DetailHref, TimeZone, StaleAfter, zero, off, by default) lists the API exchanges the same way, filtering by method, status code (0, or 100 to 599, matched exactly; any other value is ignored), service, path and request id, and, while the host does not export its API exchanges, says This app does not export API exchanges, naming Solhigson:Logs:ApiLogsToLokiEnabled. KitAppLogDetail (Id, ListHref, DetailHref, TimeZone, ApiLogHref, ShowPersonal) shows one record: its message in the kit's code block, its source, machine and request id, linked with ApiLogHref to the API exchanges of that request, each further property, the exception and its stack, and the request's first 50 records with this one marked; the user id, the address and the further properties that name a person show only with ShowPersonal, while the message, the exception and its stack are shown as written. KitApiLogDetail (Id, ListHref, TimeZone, AppLogHref) shows one exchange: its method and path, its facts, its request id, linked with AppLogHref to the application log of that request, and each side's headers and body as exported, with protected values already removed; the end user's id is not shown. Both record pages write Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store and answer a record not found with 404 and Record not found, which a page that streams answers with 200, so they must not stream. KitLogList, KitLogListBase<TRecord> and KitLogRecordPage<TValue> are the public abstract bases the four components derive from; their constructors are private protected, so an app derives nothing from them. kit.manifest.json gains the kit-logs and kit-code components, the classes kit-logs, kit-logs-current, kit-logs-message, kit-logs-method, kit-logs-muted, kit-logs-text and kit-code, and the token --kit-code-height, and loses none. To adopt: add the four pages, each with its route and a [Permission] held only by operators, since logs are one store for the whole app and each screen checks only that the viewer is signed in; keep stream rendering off the record pages; call AddSolhigsonLokiReader, naming its ServiceNames, and set Solhigson:Logs:LokiReadEnabled, Solhigson:Logs:LokiUrl, Solhigson:Logs:LokiUser and Solhigson:Logs:LokiToken, the token a read-only one (logs read alone, never the export's write credential), limited where the store allows to the app's own services and environment; for the API screen, call AddSolhigsonLogExport with its logs exporting (Solhigson:Logs:OtlpExportEnabled and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT) and Solhigson:Logs:ApiLogsToLokiEnabled; name deployment.environment.name in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, which the reader selects on; add the meter Solhigson.Admin to the host's OpenTelemetry set-up. The README lists the lines the log screens cause that an operator acts on (KitLogsFailed, KitLogsNoActor and the framework reader's SolhigsonLokiReadFailed), each with its level and what to do, and the logs instruments. Changes for a 10.5.0 app: AddSolhigsonAdmin also registers IKitLogs, keeping a seam the app registered first; the audit list's presets, More filters and time cells are drawn by the shared parts of KitPageHeader, KitFilterBar and KitTable, with the same output; the audit entry page's payload pre gains the class kit-code beside kit-audit-raw, keeping --kit-audit-raw-height; the stylesheet's .kit-audit, a.kit-audit-scope and .kit-audit-marker rules, and the user and role pages' wrapping header line, also cover the log pages, and .kit-audit-at + .kit-audit-scope now matches only inside .kit-audit. No existing type gains a public member; every type of Solhigson.Admin.Logs, and every component named above but KitPageHeader, KitFilterBar and KitTable, is new. Minor bump. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.31.0 or later. 10.5.0: the account pages (Solhigson.Admin.Account, Solhigson.Admin.Components): the sign-in page, the code page, the sign-out page, the forgot-password page, the reset-password page, the change-password page and the two-factor page, the code to scan and the shell's gate. The account seam: IKitAccount, which AddSolhigsonAdmin registers scoped over the framework's identity manager of the same type arguments, and over its two-factor manager where the app calls AddSolhigsonTwoFactor, keeping one the app registered first, is the one seam the pages call (SignInAsync, TwoFactorSignInAsync, SignOutAsync, CurrentAsync, RequestPasswordResetAsync, ResetPasswordAsync, ChangePasswordAsync, BeginEnrolmentAsync, CurrentEnrolmentAsync, ShowEnrolmentAsync, CompleteEnrolmentAsync, DisableTwoFactorAsync); the framework decides every sign-in, and the seam adds no rule. KitSignInResult carries a KitSignInOutcome (the framework's SignInOutcome values by name and number, and Failed), PendingUserId, Next (KitSignInNext: Code, ChangePassword, Enrol or Done, and None for every refusal and fault) and KitAccountMessages' sentence, one sentence for a wrong password, an unknown name and a disabled or locked account; KitAccountView holds UserId, DisplayName, HasPassword, TwoFactorEnabled, MustChangePassword, TwoFactorAvailable, CanEnrol and MustEnrol; KitReturnUrl.Safe sends every return address KitHref.Local refuses to the fallback. KitAccountOptions holds Brand, HomePath, PublicOrigin (the origin an emailed link starts with, never read from a request; null by default, and no reset link is built without it), SignInPath, CodePath, ChangePasswordPath and TwoFactorPath (the last two may be null where the app has no such page: then no page sends a user there and the step is never asked for, with one KitAccountPathNotSet Warning a process), Gate, ResetPath and ForgotPasswordPath; the host does not start on a PublicOrigin that is not an https origin alone (http on a loopback host) or a path KitHref.Local refuses. KitAccountAudit records account.signed-in, account.locked-out (the attempt that locks, at step password, code, change-password, two-factor-on or two-factor-off), account.signed-out, account.reset-requested, account.password-reset, account.password-changed, account.two-factor-enrolled and account.two-factor-disabled as security events, each naming the user as its actor (KitAuditEvent.ActorUserId) but the reset request, which reads "A visitor asked for a password reset link for Jane Doe"; a refused attempt records nothing, and account.locked-out reads "Locked out after wrong passwords or codes". Each call adds one to the counter account on the meter Solhigson.Admin (KitAccountDiagnostics), tagged method and outcome, and a reset request floor. The pages: each is a component on the app's own route, rendered on a request alone with no interactive render mode; each writes Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store before its first await, throws, saying so, under stream rendering, posts to its own path with no data-enhance, and writes no log line of its own. KitSignIn (form sign-in; ReturnUrl, ForgotHref) sends the user on by Next, and a viewer already signed in to the step they owe or to HomePath. KitTwoFactorCode (form two-factor-code; PendingUserId, ReturnUrl) completes a two-factor sign-in, a wrong code told apart from the refusals that end the sign-in. KitSignOut (form KitSignOut.FormName, sign-out) signs this device alone out on a post with a token and sends the user to SignInPath; a GET signs nobody out. KitForgotPassword (form forgot-password) says "If that address has an account, a reset link is on its way." for every address that is one, no sooner than 700 ms after the post, and mails the link KitResetLink builds from PublicOrigin and ResetPath (the query fields userId and token) through the app's IKitAccountMail. KitResetPassword (form reset-password; UserId, Token, ForgotHref) sets a new password from the link, also writing Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, ends the user's sessions through IKitSessions, signs no one in, and shows one frame for every link that does not work. KitChangePassword (form change-password; ReturnUrl, ForgotHref) changes a signed-in user's password with their current one, keeping this device signed in; a lockout signs the device out. KitTwoFactorSetup (ReturnUrl) turns two-factor on with an authenticator app, and off. Its set-up (two-factor-begin), show-the-key (two-factor-show), confirm (two-factor-confirm) and start-over (two-factor-restart) forms each ask the current password (the field password) before BeginEnrolmentAsync, ShowEnrolmentAsync or CompleteEnrolmentAsync acts, so a session alone, a stolen one among them, cannot add a device or copy the key: a wrong password counts toward lockout, and the one that locks records account.locked-out at step two-factor-on. A GET begins nothing and shows no key: CurrentEnrolmentAsync answers a pending key as KitEnrolmentOutcome.Pending, its key empty, and the key and its address are drawn only in the answer to a proved set-up, show or start-over, as the code to scan and as text in groups of four. Turning two-factor off (two-factor-disable, folded in a closed details) asks a code from the app, never the password; a wrong code counts toward lockout, and an answer whose EndSessions is set (KitTwoFactorOffResult) ends the user's sessions and signs this device out. A reset, a change, and two-factor turned on or off each records its row and tells the owner through IKitAccountMail.NotifyAsync (KitAccountNotice: PasswordReset, PasswordChanged, TwoFactorTurnedOff, TwoFactorTurnedOn); with no IKitAccountMail registered nothing is mailed, with one KitUserSeamDefault Warning a process. KitAuthFrame is the frame of the sign-in, code, sign-out, forgot-password and reset-password pages: the Brand, one h1 of its Title and the content, in one column no wider than --kit-auth-w, with no brand inside the shell. The code to scan: KitQrCode (Value, Label) draws a QR code at error correction level M as an inline svg of plain rect elements, with role img and Label as its aria-label, in --kit-qr-ink on --kit-qr-paper, black on white in both themes, at --kit-qr-size; a value too long for a code draws the label alone and writes one KitQrCodeTooLong Warning naming its length, never the value. Its encoder is QRCoder (MIT), the package's new dependency, at 1.6.0 or later, its module matrix alone. The shell's gate: before it renders anything, KitShell reads the viewer (IKitAccount.CurrentAsync) on every page it wraps, and sends a signed-in user whose password must change to ChangePasswordPath, else one who must enrol to TwoFactorPath, a post included, carrying the page's path without its query, kept out of every cache; it holds no one on those two pages or the sign-out page, for a visitor, with no request, on a re-executed error page, or for a step whose path is null; a read that throws lets the page render with one KitShellGateFailed Error; it covers the pages inside the shell only, and KitAccountOptions.Gate = false turns it off. The shared email: KitUserRow.EmailShared, which IKitUsers.GetAsync reads in one more query, says another stored account holds the user's email, so a reset the user asks for sends no link, and KitUserDetail then shows a Warn alert under its facts naming neither account. To adopt: add the seven pages, the sign-in, code, sign-out, forgot-password and reset-password pages anonymous and the change-password and two-factor pages with [Authorize]; set KitAccountOptions, its paths and PublicOrigin; rate-limit the sign-in, code, forgot-password and reset-password routes, and the sign-out, change-password and two-factor routes, and register a counter store for the framework's reset-link cap; keep the reset route's query out of request logging, and the account routes out of inbound tracing (README, Keeping the account routes out of tracing); register IKitAccountMail, queuing each mail and answering once it is queued, and IKitSessions; point the shell's SignOutAction at the sign-out page with SignOutFormName KitSignOut.FormName and no OnSignOut; guard pages outside the shell yourself; call AddSolhigsonTwoFactor and register root encryption (AddRootEncryption) for the two-factor page; an app's own IKitAccount proves the password argument in BeginEnrolmentAsync, ShowEnrolmentAsync and CompleteEnrolmentAsync and answers a pending key from CurrentEnrolmentAsync with no key; the package has no page that creates the first administrator. The README lists the log lines an operator acts on: the account seam's (KitAccountFailed, KitAccountNoOrigin, KitAccountNoResetToken), the shell's gate's (KitShellGateFailed, KitAccountPathNotSet), KitQrCodeTooLong and those the pages cause under KitUserSeams, KitAudit and the framework's Identity, Identity.Password, Identity.TwoFactor, Identity.AuthenticatorStep and Identity.AuthenticatorKey categories, the counter store's outages among them, each with its level and what to do. kit.manifest.json gains the kit-auth and kit-qr components and their classes, and the tokens --kit-auth-w, --kit-qr-ink, --kit-qr-paper and --kit-qr-size, and loses none. Changes for a 10.4.0 app: AddSolhigsonAdmin also registers IKitAccount and validates KitAccountOptions at start, keeping a seam the app registered first; KitShell's gate is on by default, so the shell reads the viewer on every page it wraps, each read one current call on the account counter, renders nothing until the gate has answered, and sends a user whose RequirePasswordChange is set, or who must enrol, to ~/account/change-password or ~/account/two-factor: an app without those pages adds them, sets ChangePasswordPath or TwoFactorPath to null, or sets Gate to false, and a layout with [StreamRendering] around the shell throws for a user the gate holds; with OnSignOut unset, the shell's sign-out form posts elsewhere (KitMenuForm.PostsElsewhere), writing its _handler field and registering no form name on the page it wraps; KitAuditOptions.ResolvedSubjectActions also holds the account.* actions by default, and KitAuditLabels words them; an app's own IKitAudit records KitAuditEvent.ActorUserId, when set, as the row's actor; with no IKitUserNotices of the app's but an IKitAccountMail, the default PasswordLinkNeededAsync (an enable of a user with no password, Send password link, Create user) sends the package's reset link where it answered false; IKitUsers.GetAsync makes one more read, the last, and a fault in it answers Failed with KitUsersFailed at step EmailShared; KitAlert lands any attribute it does not own on the alert, refusing a url; and KitField reads an inputmode or a maxlength attribute as its new parameter, so one on a kind that takes none, or one not valid, now throws, as does one in an Attributes dictionary passed whole. Of the existing types, KitAlert gains TakesFocus and Attributes, KitField gains InputMode and MaxLength, KitMenuForm gains PostsElsewhere, KitAuditEvent gains ActorUserId and KitUserRow gains EmailShared; every other type and member is new. Minor bump. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.31.0 or later. 10.4.0: the audit trail screens (Solhigson.Admin.Components, Solhigson.Admin.Auditing). The reader seam: IKitAuditReader, which AddSolhigsonAdmin registers scoped over the framework's IAuditTrailReader<TContext> for the context it is given, as it registers IKitAudit, is how the audit screens read the audit trail (Available; SearchAsync of a KitAuditSearch, answering a KitAuditPage of KitAuditRow; GetAsync of a record's id and created key, answering a KitAuditLookup of a KitAuditRecord; each answer carrying a KitAuditOutcome, Done, NotAvailable, ActorRefused, NotFound or Failed, and KitAuditMessages.For's sentence). It refuses a viewer who is not signed in before anything is read, reads the time once from the registered TimeProvider and resolves one window from the viewer's days in their zone through the framework's AuditTrailWindow, passes every filter and the cursor, answers NotAvailable with no query when no reader resolves or the context does not map AuditTrail, and throws nothing but the caller's cancellation; a fault's line names the filters set, never their values. A row's Linkable, ActorLinkable and ActorAttempted say whether a link may carry its entity id or its actor id, so text a sign-in caller typed never reaches a link, and a name a caller gave on a security event is marked as attempted. People are named for the viewer: a name a row stores shows to every viewer; an id it stores with no name is looked up in one UserAdministration.ResolveDisplayNamesAsync call a page or a record, and shows as the user's name only when the viewer's scope admits the user, else as a fragment of the id; a subject is looked up only on a user's entity type under an allow-listed action, KitAuditOptions' UserEntityTypes (User by default, beside the identity's own user class) and ResolvedSubjectActions (the users.* actions by default); a record about a user the viewer may not reach is Restricted and carries no changes, no snapshot and no address, a record's address is withheld unless the lookup names its actor for the viewer, while a record with no actor id keeps its address, which ShowIp shows to every viewer unless the record is Restricted, and a failed lookup sets NamesUnavailable. With no user-administration rules registered nothing is looked up or restricted, so the audit page's permission belongs only to roles that may see every user. KitAuditLabels gives the package's 15 audit actions a label and a verb phrase (For, Sentence, TypeInWords), so a record reads "Ada Obi changed the roles of Jane Doe", and any other action reads as the framework's AuditDisplay labels it; KitAuditEvent.SettingEntityType names the settings screen's entity type. The audit list: KitAuditList, which an app places on its own page with DetailHref (holding {id} and {created}) and an optional TimeZone, lists the records of one window newest first, a page at a time: the header says the window in the viewer's zone, with Today, Last 7 days and Last 30 days; a GET filter bar holds the days and the category, and behind More filters the action, the subject type, the subject id and the person (the query names from, to, category, action, type, id, actor and cursor), each matched exactly as stored; the table shows when, what (the action's label, linking to the record), the subject and the person, a subject linking to its history and a person to their activity only where the row allows it; a search naming a subject or a person and no day reads all time. The audit entry page: KitAuditDetail, on a page with the record's id and created key in its route, taking Id, Created, ListHref, an optional UserHref and TimeZone, and ShowIp (false unless set), shows one record: its sentence as the title, when it was written in the viewer's zone, the facts (the category, the action, the subject, the person, the source and, with ShowIp, the address), What changed and Recorded values, a masked value reading Hidden and a payload not in the stored shape shown as text in a block that scrolls inside itself; nothing in a record is ever markup; a record not found answers 404, and the page must not stream. The history links: KitSettingsEditor, KitUserDetail and KitRoleDetail gain HistoryHref, the audit page's path, with which each setting's row ends with a History link, the user page's header gains History and Activity by this person, and the role page's header gains History, kept after a delete, each to the audit list with no day; a HistoryHref that KitHref.Local refuses, or that holds ? or #, throws before any read, and with none set nothing renders. To adopt: add two pages (the audit list, a record by id and created key), each with its route and [Permission]; the record page must not stream; map AuditTrail in the context passed to AddSolhigsonAdmin; the audit trail is one trail for the whole app, so the permission decides who reads it; a name is looked up only for users the viewer's scope admits, while a name stored on a record shows to every viewer; a record about a user the viewer may not reach shows no values; an app that captures its user class adds "securitystamp" to AuditCaptureOptions.AdditionalSensitiveNamePatterns, through a pre-populated AuditCaptureOptions singleton the framework's registration leaves in place, since the defaults do not mask SecurityStamp, which the record page would show ("securitystamp" masks the secret and nothing else, where a plain "stamp" would also mask any Timestamp column); rows captured before the pattern keep the raw stamp, so an app that has captured its user class adds the pattern, then rotates every user's security stamp (UserManager.UpdateSecurityStampAsync) before it grants the audit permission, which ends every open session at the next stamp check; an app never opts Identity's user-token, user-login or user-claim types into capture, since their values are credentials no pattern masks and their records are not restricted; add any other user class name, beside the identity's own, to KitAuditOptions.UserEntityTypes and its own safe user actions to ResolvedSubjectActions; pass TimeZone; ShowIp is off by default; pass HistoryHref to the settings, user and role pages. The README lists each log line the reader seam writes (KitAuditReaderNoActor, KitAuditReaderSearchFailed, KitAuditReaderGetFailed, KitAuditReaderUnresolved) and each line the screens' reads cause under AuditTrailReader, UserAdministration and the users seam, its level and what to do; the screens write no line of their own. The kit: KitNotice, given a KitNoticeMessage (KitNoticeMessage.Landed or NotLanded, a blank text or step throwing), says a post's answer in one message at the foot of the screen that rises in, stays (--kit-notice-dwell, --kit-notice-long-dwell) and leaves on its own, in CSS alone, and is drawn only inside KitShell, which tells it to a screen reader through two live regions that kit.notice.js fills; KitButton gains Answer (KitButtonAnswer: None, Landed, a ring in the success colour, or Failed, a sideways nudge), drawn on the render that answers a post, changing neither the button's colour, text nor size, and still under reduced motion; kit.forms.js removes every notice and both answer classes as it marks a post's submitter busy, so the next answer plays; KitFilterBar gains Enhance, true unless set, false for a bar holding a field named after a form's own member, such as action, which then submits as a plain form; kit-facts is the facts list the audit record page and the user page share; kit.manifest.json gains the kit-audit, kit-facts and kit-notice names, the kit-btn-landed, kit-btn-nudged, kit-gallery-notices, kit-role-history and kit-user-history classes, the component token --kit-audit-raw-height (the raw payload block's height, the measure unless set) and the tokens --kit-d-flash, --kit-flash-spread, --kit-flash-ring, --kit-flash-ring-end, --kit-d-nudge, --kit-nudge-1, --kit-nudge-2, --kit-nudge-3, --kit-d-notice, --kit-d-notice-leave, --kit-notice-rise, --kit-notice-dwell, --kit-notice-long-dwell, --kit-z-skip and --kit-z-float, and loses none; every new duration token is 0ms under reduced motion. Changes for a 10.3.0 app: AddSolhigsonAdmin also registers IKitAuditReader and, when the app registers no TimeProvider, TimeProvider.System, each kept when the app registered it first; KitHead also links kit.notice.js, with the page's nonce as its other scripts; KitShell renders two empty, visually hidden live regions, a status and an alert, after its main region on every page; the user page's facts list also carries the kit-facts class, its kit-user-facts class kept; and the header line of the user and role pages, and of the new-user and new-role screens, is a flex row that wraps, spaced by its gap, so a back link after a wrapped email or group takes its own line. Minor bump: every type and member is new but for those changes. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.29.0 or later.
